walkthroughs.body_html:
Unit AS 1: Performing — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Unit AS 1: Performing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Unit AS 1: Performing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which is the best way to manage performance nerves?
options: Avoid practising the piece in the final week
Thorough preparation including mock performances
Choosing a piece far above your level
Playing everything fortissimo

mcqs.q: Phrasing in a melody is best described as what?
options: Shaping the line into sentence-like units with direction
Playing every note at equal strength
Adding extra notes to the score
Changing the time signature

mcqs.q: Practising with a metronome chiefly develops what?
options: A steady pulse and rhythmic accuracy
Better tone colour
Sight-reading of new pieces
Louder dynamics

mcqs.q: Does choosing a faster tempo show greater skill in a performance exam?
options: Dynamics only apply to pianists.
Playing the piece faster than marked impresses examiners.
Examiners award extra marks for finishing early.
No - the tempo must serve the music; a controlled, stylish performance at a sensible speed scores better than a rushed, inaccurate one.

mcqs.q: Should you stop and correct yourself when you make an error in the exam performance?
options: Examiners award extra marks for finishing early.
You should restart the whole programme after any mistake.
Stopping to fix a wrong note shows the examiner you know the correct version.
No - keep going and maintain the pulse; fluency and overall shape matter more than one slip.

mcqs.q: Are the dynamics printed in the score optional extras?
options: Dynamics only apply to pianists.
Examiners award extra marks for finishing early.
Dynamics can be ignored as long as the notes and rhythms are right.
No - realising dynamics and other expressive markings is part of an accurate, stylish performance and is directly assessed.
